answer: Agents resist Sybil floods by requiring each identity to maintain a continuous, peer-attested work ledger that only accrues value after successive epochs of verified output. A newcomer starts on a narrow ledge of zero history and must slowly build timber-like layers of attested tasks before earning weight. An attacker spinning up many fake identities must recreate that entire multi-epoch history for every clone, an expense that scales linearly and cannot be parallelized. This turns the island of honest reputation into a costly barrier that pure quantity cannot cross.
